properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-29: after #622 made TemporalFact.subject_id the stored twin of HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT, record_finding's "was this edge already present?" read, taken after the upsert, reported the call's own new edge as already present; a constructor must read presence BEFORE the node write whenever the store draws twin edges inside it
properties.statement: OBSERVED on PR #623 (fix/decision-tools-draw-echo-and-name), after merging main at cc3dbd0 (#622, stored twins): the new class test a_constructor_names_every_edge_it_drew failed in CI for record_finding with edges_already_present ["req:a-need HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT fact:a-finding"] and edges_drawn missing it. Locally, before the merge, the same test passed. CAUSE, measured by reading crates/reflow2-core/src/twins.rs and schema/temporal.yaml: subject_id carries twin_of { edge: HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT }, so upsert_node draws the edge itself; the handler's presence check ran after the upsert and found the edge the call had just drawn. FIX in the same PR: drawn_edges gained `record(from, relation, to, was_present)` and record_finding reads presence BEFORE the upsert. THE LESSON FOR THE INVARIANT: "name every edge the call drew" needs the before-state of every edge the store may draw implicitly — any twin_of property a constructor writes is such an edge, so a new twin declaration can silently change what a constructor's reply says. The class test (diffing the export before and after) is what caught it, which is the argument for pinning the invariant over every constructor rather than per tool.
